# Plan: overnight autonomous SPE rounds, starting at round 5

The situation does not give round 4's metrics or costs. So this plan takes every round 5 number from `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml` and from the "Proposed for round 5" table in `spe/spec/spec.md`.

## What your message authorizes

- I take your message as approval to run rounds 5 and later without you. I will log that approval in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`.
- You will not see the plans for round 6 and later before they run. Each of those prediction files will set `author: "Claude, autonomous, under the user's 2026-10-21 overnight instruction"`. That label tells you no person reviewed them.
- I will make local commits only. I will not push, open PRs, deploy, or send anything. Commit messages will not mention Claude.
- I will stay on the current branch and will not rewrite any earlier commit or tag.

## Defaults I am choosing (logged in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`, owner: user)

| ID | Decision | Default |
|---|---|---|
| D-ON1 | Round cap | Rounds 5 to 8 at most. |
| D-ON2 | Time cap | No new round starts after 05:30 local. All work stops by 07:00. |
| D-ON3 | Spend cap | Each round may spend up to 1.5 times round 4's measured cost. The whole night may spend up to 4 times round 4's cost. Any trial that would cross a cap is skipped and logged. |
| D-ON4 | What counts as a match | A cell matches if it falls inside the tolerance used in the r04 prediction log. If r04 set no tolerance, the default is 10 percentage points for rates and 15% for counts and costs. |
| D-ON5 | Stop-rule count | The "3 matching rounds in a row" count includes rounds 3 and 4 as they are recorded in `spe/prediction-log.md`. |
| D-ON6 | Proposals I cannot settle | If a proposal needs your judgment, I reject it for now and log it as open. I do not pick an answer for you. |

## Each round (shown for rNN = r05, the same steps repeat for later rounds)

### 1. Specify
- I will save `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md` with your overnight message, copied verbatim. For round 6 and later the transcript will say "No new user input" and will quote the overnight message again.
- I will add a round 5 requirement table to `spe/spec/spec.md` with the columns ID, Requirement, Source, and Test. Every row from r04's "Proposed for round 5" table will be adopted or rejected with a one-line reason. Rows can cite r04 failure IDs from `spe/failures.md`.
- If every configuration passed everything in r04, round 5 will add harder tasks or stricter graders. It will not repeat r04 unchanged.
- Commit: `SPE r05 specify`.

### 2. Predict
- I will build a table with one row per metric and one column per configuration. Every cell will hold a number with a one-line Why. Each row will start from round 4's measured value. I will move a number only when I can state a reason, and each row will name its grader check.
- Each configuration will change one thing compared with the baseline.
- Predictions will be point values. Tolerances will be no wider than r04's, so a vaguer prediction cannot pass as a match.
- I will copy the plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`. I will write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` with round, date, author, configs, numbers, a Why for each number, and `same_as_last_round`. The file will start with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.`
- Commit: `SPE r05 predict: <one-line summary>`. This commit happens before any harness work.

### 3. Evaluate (harness)
- I will copy `spe/evals/harness/r04-workflow.js` to `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js` and set `const ROUND = 5`. Prompt text will not contain any round number written by hand.
- Gates must all pass before launch:
  1. Grader selftest. The oracle answer passes, and an empty answer and a wrong answer both fail.
  2. Control regrade. I regrade r04 with the round 5 graders. If a grader changed, I will put the original and regraded numbers side by side.
  3. Dry run on 2 or 3 cells. Every trial matches its schema, and no trial reads graders, answers, or predictions.
- I will write an unmeasured cost estimate into the plan before launch and check it against D-ON3.
- Commit: `SPE r05 evaluate (harness)`.

### 4. Evaluate (run)
- I will launch the Workflow and wait for its completion notice. I will not poll.
- Code checks run first. Judges grade only what code cannot check.
- I will scan transcripts and void any trial that peeked.
- Cells that land on the split line get extra trials, up to the cap.
- The run ends with failure analysis and a completeness critic.
- Commit: `SPE r05 evaluate (results): <headline>`.

### 5. Learn
- In `spe/prediction-log.md` I will fill the columns Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under the table, "Which Why broke" will quote each missed Why and name the wrong assumption. I will say plainly if "same as last round" beat my predictions.
- In `spe/failures.md` I will add each new F-numbered failure type with its name, kind, round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. A grader bug found after the run counts as a failure.
- I will add a "Proposed for round 6" table to the spec and write `spe/predictions/r05-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- I will update `spe/README.md`.
- Commit: `SPE r05 learn: <one-line summary>`. Then I will add the tag `spe-r05`.

### 6. Continue or stop
I will check the stop and halt rules below. If none of them applies, I will start round 6 at step 1.

## Stop rules (finish cleanly and write the morning report)
- Predictions have matched results for 3 rounds in a row under D-ON4 and D-ON5.
- Round 8 is done, or it is past 05:30.
- The proposals left for the next round all need your decisions.

## Halt rules (stop at once, commit what is safe, and report)
- A spend cap from D-ON3 would be crossed.
- An answer key leaked, or a trial read graders, answers, or predictions and voiding it would leave a cell empty.
- A grader is broken. That means the selftest or the control regrade fails and I cannot fix it in the specify step.
- A saved prediction would need an edit after a trial has run.
- A decision needs your judgment and blocks the round.
- A tool, auth, or permission failure blocks a step.

## Things I will not do
- I will not push, deploy, send messages, or touch remote systems.
- I will not edit any saved `rNN.yaml` after its trials run.
- I will not change graders between the gates and the results commit.
- I will not delete or move earlier rounds' files, commits, or tags.

## Morning report (in chat, also summarized in `spe/README.md`)
- Each round's headline, for example "r05: config B beat baseline on pass rate, 3 of 4 rows matched."
- A prediction accuracy table for r03 through the last round. It shows cells matched out of cells predicted, and whether "same as last round" did better.
- Spend for each round and the total, compared with the D-ON3 caps, plus any skipped trials.
- New failure IDs.
- Open decisions from `spe/spec/disagreements.md`, including D-ON1 to D-ON6, for you to confirm or change.
- Why the loop ended, citing the exact stop or halt rule.
- Confirmation that every commit is local and nothing was pushed.
